title: Authored DSA 5 rule
description: One machine-checkable shape for an authored rule file under specs/rules/. Carries mechanical encoding plus provenance and no rule text (Data Policy, AGENTS.md). This schema is the contract the combat engine (ADR-0008) consumes. A file is either one Optolith-identified rule or one page of chapter rules — see `#/$defs/ruleId`.

ruleId.description: An authored file's own id. Two disjoint namespaces. **Optolith ids** (`SA_`/`ADV_`/`DISADV_`/`COND_`/`CT_` + digits) name an ability, advantage, disadvantage, Zustand or Kampftechnik, and are the join key hero exports already use (ADR-0007). **Chapter ids** (`CHAP_` + a PascalCase page slug) name a *page of chapter rules* that binds anyone in the situation it describes, ability or not — mounted combat, Beengte Umgebung, multiple defences. Optolith has no id for those, and the app hardcoded their constants in Swift because the corpus had nowhere to put them, which is exactly what ADR-0008 says should be data. The two namespaces cannot collide by construction: every Optolith id ends in digits and every chapter id ends in letters. The slug is the `source.url` page stem, ASCII-folded (see `scripts/rules_lint/lint.py`, which enforces the derivation) — so the id is a stable handle to one page, checkable against the provenance already in the file rather than against a registry that could drift.

optolithId.description: An Optolith id only — the pre-chapter-rule `ruleId` pattern, unchanged. `excludes` keeps it: an excludes edge is a Kampfrunde-combination ban between two selectable maneuvers, and a chapter rule is never selected, so a chapter id on that side of the edge would be meaningless rather than merely unused.

subgroup.description: The maneuver slot this rule occupies, mirroring `rules.subgroup_id` (ADR-0008). A chapter rule (`CHAP_` id) is always `none` — it is a situation, not something a hero selects in a Kampfrunde — and `lint.py` enforces that, so a chapter page cannot silently claim a Basismanöver slot.

ruleset.description: Which set of rules this one belongs to, and therefore when the engine applies it (ADR-0009). `core` is a standard rule of the Regelwerk and is always active. `focus.<slug>` is a Fokus-Regel — an optional rule the Regelwerk prints as optional — and applies only to a hero who has that slug switched on (`Hero.fokusRules`). `house.<slug>` is a table's own rule and works the same way. Required on every authored rule and deliberately without a default: `core` is the common case, but defaulting to it would make an unmarked Fokus-Regel apply to everyone, which is the failure this field exists to prevent — the one an author is least likely to notice, because the rule then works. A `focus.`/`house.` slug must also be glossed in `specs/rules/vocabulary.yaml`, the same registration `gmFlag` and the actionEconomy tokens carry, so the set of optional rules is itself data rather than a hand-maintained Swift enum. The slug is camelCase and carries no prose (Data Policy).

note.description: English, non-prose annotation of which clause/mechanic this rule's authoring encodes — never German rule text (Data Policy) and never a substitute for `source`. ASCII-only and length-capped so it cannot carry smuggled rule prose the way a free-form field could. **Convention (Task 4 fix round 1, I-3): identify the clause by position and mechanism, never restate its content.** "Clause 3 - opponent-side outcome with no hero-side number, promoted to a reminder" is a note; "the shield is destroyed once its structure points reach 0" is a translation of the clause, i.e. the Data Policy back door a free-text field leaves open — and a `reminder` effect, which has no field but `note`, is exactly where that pressure lands. Where a note must record a clause the grammar cannot express, prefix it `UNENCODED:` so `grep -r UNENCODED specs/rules` enumerates the whole debt. A second marker, on the rule-root note only: prefix it `UNCLEAR-RULESET:` when the page does not state which set the rule belongs to and `ruleset` was therefore guessed as `core` (ADR-0009 requires the guess to run in the visible direction; this requires it to be visible *as a guess*). Greppable exactly like `UNENCODED:` and `DISAGREEMENT:`, and a marker rather than prose: name the ambiguity, never restate the clause.

url.description: Provenance URL. `format: uri` is not enforced by the default jsonschema FormatChecker (no `uri` checker registered without the `rfc3987` extra, which this repo does not add), so this is a real, enforced `pattern` instead of a decorative `format`.

title.description: The page's own title, in its display spelling (umlauts, spaces). Required on a chapter rule (`CHAP_` id) and meaningless on an Optolith one: a chapter rule has no `rules_i18n` row, because there is no Optolith entry behind it, so a breakdown line citing one would have nothing to render but its id (ADR-0009). `build_db.py` writes it into the chapter rule's `rules` row, and the UI explains the number with that title, a link to `source.url`, and the rule's own authored `reminder` notes. This is the one field in a chapter file that holds German, so it is not guarded by a length cap alone: `scripts/rules_lint/lint.py` requires it to ASCII-fold to exactly the slug the id derives from the URL. That is ADR-0009's own argument for allowing the field — the id *is* the page title, ASCII-folded — made mechanical. A sentence folds to something that is not the page slug and is rejected; only the display spelling of a name the repository already holds can pass (Data Policy).

excludes.description: Rule ids this rule cannot be combined with in the same Kampfrunde (e.g. Sturmangriff excludes Finte). Optolith ids only — see `#/$defs/optolithId`.

effects.description: The rule's encoding. At least one row: a rule that reduces to zero effects is not an encoding, it is a refusal to encode -- and two agents that both return nothing agree with each other and lint clean (Task 6 fix round 1, C3). Every authored rule in the corpus has at least one row, so the bound costs nothing and turns a systematic authoring failure from a clean run into a loud one. A clause the grammar cannot express is a `reminder` with an `UNENCODED:` note, never an empty list.

type.description: The closed nine-case effect union (ADR-0008). Unhandled cases are a compile error in the engine rather than a silent no-op, so this enum is non-negotiable.

tier.description: The ability's Stufe, where the effect scales per tier (e.g. a shiftSteps parameterOverride multiplies by tier). Range covers the corpus's longest ladders (ADV_24/DISADV_27 run to VII).

note.description: English, non-prose annotation of which clause/mechanic this effect encodes — never German rule text (Data Policy). ASCII-only and length-capped so it cannot carry smuggled rule prose the way a free-form field could. Same convention and `UNENCODED:` prefix as the rule-root `note` above; the numbers live in the effect's own fields, so a note that repeats them is restating the clause rather than locating it.

when.description: Preconditions, ANDed together. The closed eleven-predicate set (ADR-0008), each with its own value shape so a malformed predicate value (e.g. `{mounted: banana}`) fails to lint rather than silently no-op in the engine. Ten predicates cover the combat corpus; the eleventh, `gmFlag`, carries a non-combat precondition on an ADV/DISADV/COND rule (e.g. "at a known location", "sleepwalked last night") as a GM-adjudicated toggle rather than letting the rule silently become unconditional (ADR-0008's "never to silence" rule).

combatTechnique.description: combatTechnique(in:) — membership in a set of combat technique ids (CT_...).

targetState.description: targetState(_) — the opponent carries this Zustand/Status id.

targetSize.description: targetSize(≤) — opponent size at most this category, matching the existing ModifierContext.groesse scale (0=winzig .. 4=riesig).

attribute.description: attribute(_, ≥) — a single stat-name/threshold pair, e.g. {gs: 4} for GS ≥ 4.

runUp.description: runUp(≥) — required run-up distance in Schritt.

weaponReach.description: The hero's weapon reach, matching WeaponReach's raw values (Hesindion/Models/CombatManeuver.swift).

defenseCount.description: defenseCount(≥) — number of defenses already made this Kampfrunde.

armorAtMost.description: armorAtMost(_) — opponent/hero RS at most this value.

offHandWeapon.description: The check uses the off-hand weapon.

gmFlag.description: gmFlag(<slug>) — a GM-adjudicated condition with no mechanical predicate (e.g. "at a known location", "ambush detection", "principles violated"). The engine surfaces it as a GM toggle rather than applying it automatically, exactly as ModifierContext.targetIsSurprised already works under ADR-0005. The slug is a constrained camelCase identifier so rule prose cannot enter through it.

stacks.description: Explicit opt-out of the default rule that effects from different abilities stack (ADR-0008). Omit (or true) to stack normally; false marks an effect as participating in a 'strongest applies' exception that must otherwise be stated in the data (e.g. two `set` overrides of the same parameter).

target.description: modifier: which value the modifier moves. Closed set, established against the 79 existing effect rows before any rule was authored (ADR-0008). `duration`, `offHandPenalty`, `shieldPaBonus`, `anaesthesia` and `defense` were pruned from this set (Task 3 fix round 1): they were exactly the legacy attribute names the migration moved onto other effect types (`recovery.attribute`, `parameterOverride.parameter`, `stateGain.state`, `actionEconomy.forbids`) and zero of the corpus's effects use them as a `modifier.target` — leaving them invited authoring `modifier target: shieldPaBonus` instead of the correct `parameterOverride`.

scope.description: modifier: the domain the modifier applies within. Closed set, established against the 79 existing effect rows (ADR-0008).

side.description: modifier: whose check this modifies. Default `hero`. `opponent` is display-only — it states a number for the GM (as CombatManeuver.infoText() already does for Finte), so it does not reverse ADR-0005.

value.description: modifier: the flat numeric modifier. recovery: the amount recovered (with `operation`/`per`).

parameter.description: parameterOverride: dotted path of the named DSA constant being overridden, e.g. `defense.multiplePenaltyPerStep`, `reach.matrix`, or a wildcard family such as `zone.*`.

set.description: parameterOverride: replace the named parameter's value outright (e.g. Meisterparade: set defense.multiplePenaltyPerStep = -2).

shiftSteps.description: parameterOverride: shift the named parameter by this many steps, scaled by the effect's `tier` (e.g. Unterlaufen: shiftSteps reach.matrix by tier).

scale.description: parameterOverride: multiply the named parameter by this factor (e.g. Gezielter Angriff: scale zone.* by 0.5).

add.description: dice: a damage/value expression to add, evaluated against the check context (e.g. "2 + ceil(self.gs / 2)", "1W6"). Free-form because the corpus's dice formulas are not closed the way effect types and predicates are.

recipient.description: dice: who the added damage lands on. Defaults to the attack's own target; `defenderShield` covers Schildspalter (SA_59), which lands on the defender's shield instead. Non-hero recipients are display-only, per ADR-0005.

grants.description: actionEconomy: what the ability grants (e.g. "freeAction", "extraManeuver"). Not an enum — the vocabulary is not finite over 232 rules, and closing it would make every novel ability a schema PR, the trade ADR-0008 refused for `dice.add`. It is nonetheless a *slug*, not prose: the camelCase pattern below is what stops `grants: "der Gegner erhält einen Passierschlag"` from linting clean, which the unconstrained `type: string` allowed (Task 4 fix round 1, Q4). Every token must also be registered with an English gloss in `specs/rules/vocabulary.yaml`, which `lint.py` enforces — a new token is then a reviewable one-line diff rather than an invisible invention, and that registry becomes the enum once the corpus stops growing.

forbids.description: actionEconomy: what the ability removes (e.g. "allActions" for Handlungsunfähig-like incapacitation, "defense" for a lost defence). A separate field from `grants` because a removal encoded as a grant reads backwards. Same slug pattern and same `vocabulary.yaml` registration as `grants`.

skill.description: probe: which skill/check the probe is made against, when it is not simply the acting check (e.g. "Selbstbeherrschung").

state.description: stateGain: the Zustand/Status id granted (StateCatalog id), e.g. "betaeubung".

level.description: stateGain: the level granted, for leveled Zustände (I-IV).

action.description: legality: the otherwise-illegal action this effect makes legal, e.g. "basismanoever+spezialmanoever". Optional — some legality grants need no further qualification. Same registration requirement as `grants`/`forbids` (`specs/rules/vocabulary.yaml`). The pattern allows `+`-joined camelCase segments, because this field's own worked example is a *combination* of two named things; a naive camelCase-only pattern would have rejected the schema's own example.

attribute.description: recovery: which stat is recovered (e.g. "LE", "AsP", "KP"). Free-form: not closed by ADR-0008.
